title: The Ledger of the Lower Danube
premise: On the lower Danube in the winter before the armistice, Wendell Oyelaran keeps the ledgers of her father's print shop and the secrets of a city where every faction prints its own version of the truth. When a scarred stranger named Ilse arrives with a letter in the handwriting of Anton Vasilescu — the revolutionary printer officially drowned two years ago — Wendell discovers her father helped fake the death to protect a list of names that could damn the coming victors. As armies converge and the armistice nears, Wendell must choose between protecting her father and setting the record straight, ultimately printing the true ledger in a final overnight run as the armistice is signed, knowing it may cost her family everything but will outlast every victor's history.
about_author: Marguerite Ishikawa is the pen name of a former archival conservator who spent a decade restoring water-damaged ledgers from river towns along the Danube. She writes historical fiction about the people who kept records when keeping records was a dangerous act.

chapters.title: The Weight of Blank Paper
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. On a frozen morning in the print shop, Wendell sets type for a proclamation she knows is false, practicing the silences her father taught her. Establishes the city's factions, the shop's precarious neutrality, and her gift for reading handwriting. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath competence.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Loading Door
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Ilse arrives after dark, soaked from the river, carrying a letter in Anton Vasilescu's unmistakable hand — the man officially dead two years. Wendell hides her before her father returns and watches his face collapse. Emotional beat: shock cracking open a carefully sealed household.

chapters.title: What My Father Burned
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell confronts her father, who admits only fragments: Anton is alive, there is a ledger of names, and the faked drowning was his doing. He refuses to say whose names. Emotional beat: the first real rupture between daughter and father.

chapters.title: The Hand That Keeps Writing
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse reveals she was Anton's apprentice and courier; the letter is a summons to a meeting upstream. She doesn't fully trust the Oyelaran family either. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two women who have both survived by misdirection.

chapters.title: Ink and Ice
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The journey upriver by barge, passing checkpoints of three different armies. Wendell memorizes which officers read which papers, realizing documents themselves decide who lives. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Man Who Was a Corpse
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The meeting with Anton in a mill outside a half-ruined town. He is older, half-crippled, and unrepentant: the ledger exists to prove who ordered the reprisals, and it must be printed before the armistice freezes the official story. Emotional beat: awe curdling into suspicion of his motives.

chapters.title: Names in the Margin
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell sees a page of the ledger and finds her father's name in the margin — not as victim but as witness to something he never confessed. She copies it secretly. Emotional beat: betrayal and the first pull toward truth over loyalty.

chapters.title: The Committee of the Victorious
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. In the occupied capital, the armistice commission begins writing its official history, commissioning print shops — including, fatefully, the Oyelaran shop. Ilse infiltrates as a translator. Emotional beat: the enemy is not soldiers but the machinery of narrative.

chapters.title: A Summons Written in My Father's Hand
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Back home, Wendell discovers her father has been summoned by the commission — they know about the faked drowning. He plans to confess and take all blame alone. Emotional beat: Wendell realizes protecting him means exposing the truth he wants buried.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Daughter
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell seeks out a disgraced archivist, Madame Kertész, who teaches her how records are forged, suppressed, and authenticated. Wendell learns to prove handwriting, watermarks, and dates. Emotional beat: empowerment through craft.

chapters.title: Ilse's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Anton asks Ilse to steal the commission's draft history so the ledger can be printed with its pages interleaved. Ilse agrees but hides that she once betrayed Anton's network under interrogation. Emotional beat: guilt compounding into a debt she intends to pay.

chapters.title: The Raid on the Shop
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Soldiers search the print shop; Wendell hides the ledger page in a forme of locked type and watches an officer nearly discover it. Her father is taken for questioning. Emotional beat: terror, then cold resolve.

chapters.title: Confession, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse witnesses the father's interrogation and learns the commission already has its own forged version of events — one that blames the victims. She realizes Anton's ledger is the only counterweight. Emotional beat: the stakes become historical, not personal.

chapters.title: Two Hands, One Page
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell and Ilse compare the commission's forgery with the ledger and find a shared source: the forger learned from the same master — Anton's own former teacher, now the commission's chief historian. Emotional beat: the sickening recognition that truth and lie share a lineage.

chapters.title: The Night Ferry
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The women ferry Anton's ledger pages across the frozen river while patrols sweep the banks; Ilse's old interrogator is among the officers. She chooses not to run. Emotional beat: courage as a decision made repeatedly.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell visits her father in custody and offers him the choice: let her print the truth and name him, or stay silent and let the forgery stand. He rages, then breaks, giving her the final missing page. Emotional beat: love that survives honesty.

chapters.title: The Forger's Signature
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. With Kertész's methods, Wendell proves the commission's history is forged and prepares the evidence to be bound into the printed edition itself — the truth hidden inside the victors' own book. Emotional beat: audacity, the plan's elegant danger.

chapters.title: Anton's Second Death
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Anton is captured; the commission offers to spare him if he denounces the ledger as forgery. He refuses and dies in custody, and Ilse smuggles out his final letter — in the same handwriting that started everything. Emotional beat: grief transformed into obligation.

chapters.title: The Overnight Run
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The armistice signing is hours away. Wendell, Ilse, and the shop's remaining workers set the true edition through the night — locked doors, extinguished lamps, type set by touch. Emotional beat: the whole novel's craft and silence converging into action.

chapters.title: Signatures at Dawn
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. As delegates sign the armistice, copies of the interleaved edition circulate through the commission itself; the chief historian discovers the forgery exposed in his own printed book. Wendell is arrested mid-run but the copies are already moving. Emotional beat: triumph inseparable from peril.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell stands before a tribunal, using Kertész's methods to authenticate the ledger publicly, naming her father among the witnesses. Ilse testifies about her own betrayal, completing her debt. Emotional beat: truth spoken plainly at last, at maximum cost.

chapters.title: The Ledger of the Lower Danube
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, epilogue. A year later, the shop prints under Wendell's name; her father, released, sets type beside her in silence that no longer means hiding. A copy of the true edition rests in the national archive, water-stained and stubborn. Emotional beat: memory outlasting victors; identity chosen, not inherited.
